legend.status.field|section|removed-feature: what happens when the key is present: absent = not declared, silently ignored; accepted = parsed and used; deprecated = loads with a warning/auto-migration; rejected = Build()/startup fails
legend.status.value: whether the listed value or syntax loads (absent = parsed but meaningless / taken literally)
legend.status.constraint: what happens to a config that hits the described condition (accepted = still loads, rejected = fails to load or crashes)
legend.perVersionKeys: keys that load without error in that tag; keys whose mere presence fails the load are in perVersionRejectedKeys
legend.jsonDecoding: all sections are decoded with Go encoding/json: key names match case-insensitively and undeclared keys are dropped silently

items.detail: Map of environment variables that Config.Build applies with os.Setenv before post-processing and every other section (merged key-by-key across multiple config files); values must be JSON strings, and it does not affect `env:NAME` address/port references, which are resolved earlier while the JSON is decoded.

Scheduled geo-asset refresh: `cron` (robfig standard 5-field or @descriptor, validated at load) reloads the geoip/geosite registries, and when `assets` is non-empty each run first downloads every `url` through the outbound tagged `outbound` and atomically swaps it into `file`; without `cron` the section is a no-op.

items.detail: Legacy bridge/portal reverse works in v26.3.27; from v26.7.28 any non-null `reverse` object, even `{}`, fails with PrintRemovedFeatureError("legacy reverse" -> "VLESS Reverse Proxy").
A non-empty top-level `transport` object fails the load in every tag (an empty `{}` or null is tolerated), so the editor must never emit it.
Configs are decoded by Go encoding/json, so key names match case-insensitively (`fakedns` and `fakeDns` are the same key and collide) and misspelled/undeclared keys are dropped without any error.

Comments load by default in every tag, but from v26.7.28 a node started with env xray.json.strict / XRAY_JSON_STRICT=true decodes plain RFC 8259 JSON and a commented config fails; the flag is read at process start, so the config's own `env` cannot set it.
The running core refuses to start when its version is below `min` or above `max`, so an editor can stamp `version.min` on configs that rely on keys introduced in a later tag.

Up to v26.7.28 `{tag, transportLayer}` chains through another outbound (empty tag errors, transportLayer:true is rewritten into sockopt.dialerProxy, and setting both proxySettings.tag and sockopt.dialerProxy is a load error); v26.9.9 rejects any non-null proxySettings, including `{}`.

items.detail: An empty-string listen parses as an empty domain and crashes the build on `Domain()[0]` before v26.9.9, so the editor must omit the key rather than write "".
Listening on any other domain fails, and `port` is mandatory unless protocol is tun or listen is a Unix socket (where port is dropped).
Not declared on InboundDetourConfig in any tag, so it is silently ignored.
New in v26.7.28: when the original destination is an IP matching this list, sniffing results do not override the destination; invalid rules or unknown geoip codes fail the load.

Semantics changed in v26.7.28: a plain entry that meant an exact domain now matches as a substring (use `full:` to keep exact), routing-style prefixes and geosite lists now work, and a bad regexp or unknown geosite code now fails the load instead of being skipped at runtime.
Case-insensitive in every tag (https/ssl alias tls, fakedns+others collapses to fakedns); any other string fails the load.
Two inbounds or two outbounds sharing a non-empty tag fail at startup with "existing tag found" in every tag.

items.detail: New in v26.9.9 (string or array): the rule matches only when the core itself runs on one of the listed OSes, resolved once at startup, and it counts as an effective condition.
When a rule carries both keys, v26.3.27 appends them while v26.7.28+ silently discards `domain`, so the editor should write only one of them.
A leading `!` on any IP rule (plain CIDR or geoip) fails as an invalid IP in v26.3.27 but is a negated match from v26.7.28 via the shared geodata parser.

items.path: routing.rules[].domain|domains, dns.servers[].domains, dns.hosts keys: ext-site: prefix
items.detail: `ext-site:file:code` is new in v26.7.28; in v26.3.27 it is taken as a literal substring and never matches, and from v26.7.28 an empty geosite attribute (`geosite:cn@`) is a load error.
A rule with neither outboundTag nor balancerTag fails, and a balancerTag that names no balancer fails at router start, in every tag (outboundTag wins if both are set).

A rule whose only keys are ruleTag/outboundTag/balancerTag/webhook (or empty lists) fails with "this rule has no effective fields", so a catch-all needs a condition such as network "tcp,udp" or port "0-65535".
Attribute values are compiled with regexp.MustCompile when the router starts, so an invalid Go regexp crashes the core in every tag.

v26.3.27: last balancer with a tag wins; duplicate ruleTags coexist
v26.7.28: last balancer with a tag wins; duplicate ruleTags coexist

items.detail: Before v26.9.9 Router.Init built rules without duplicate checks (only the API AddRule path checked); v26.9.9 routes startup through ReloadRules and fails on a repeated non-empty ruleTag or balancer tag.
Case-insensitive in every tag; an unknown value silently becomes AsIs rather than failing.
RouterConfig only declares rules, domainStrategy and balancers in all three tags (and DNSConfig has no domainMatcher either), so the key is silently ignored.

items.detail: Case-insensitive and unchanged; an unknown value silently falls back to UseIP.

From v26.7.28 host keys go through the shared domain-rule parser, so ext-domain:/ext-site: keys work (v26.3.27 treats them as literal full domains) and the conf-level check for empty `domain:`/`regexp:`/`keyword:`/`full:` keys is gone; values are unchanged (IP, IP list, or a domain for CNAME-like proxying).
Server schemes are identical across the three tags; a server object without `address` and a non-IP clientIp (server or global) fail the load.
A geo code or file that is missing from the node's asset directory fails the load in every tag, so the editor cannot fully validate these without knowing the node's .dat files.
Unchanged: any other value fails log startup; `loglevel` accepts debug/info/warning/error/none and silently treats unknown values as warning.
A Unix-socket api.listen fails at startup in v26.3.27 (plain TCP listen) and is supported from v26.7.28; in every tag api.tag is required and unknown `services` names are silently ignored.
A metrics object with neither `tag` nor `listen` fails the load in every tag.
Unchanged: the declared key is `fakeDns` (matched case-insensitively), and if dns.servers contains "fakedns" without this section a default pool is synthesized from dns.queryStrategy.
Any Address-typed field and any port string may be `env:NAME`, read from the process environment while the JSON is decoded (before the new top-level `env` section is applied).
